classification.summary: GMX v1 Vault (deployed 2021): cross-contract reentrancy let short-position accounting inflate GLP price before redemption. Aged-code counterexample - v1 code was ~4 years old.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

sources.note: onchain review (exploit tx now identified from the DeFiHackLabs PoC: 0x0b8cd648fb585bc3d421fc02150013eab79e211ef8d1c68100f2820ce90a4712, arbitrum block 355878385, 2025-07-09T12:22:28Z, sender 0xdf3340a436c27655ba62f8281565c9925c3a5221 -- the attacker's leveraged-long open; the sequence continues with keeper execution 0x28a000501ef8e3364b0e7f573256b04b87d9a8e8173410c869004b987bf0beef, decrease order 0x20abfeff0206030986b05422080dc9e81dbb53a662fbc82461a47418decc49af and keeper execution 0x1f00da742318ad1807b6ea8283bfe22b4a8ab0bc98fe428fbfe443746a4a7353). GMX v1 Vault 0x489ee077994B6658eAfA855C308275EAd8097C4A was created at arbitrum block 227091, 2021-08-31T07:35:06Z. It is not a proxy: the runtime bytecode contains zero DELEGATECALL opcodes, there is no EIP-1967 Upgraded event on it, and eth_getCode returns a byte-identical runtime at the creation block and at the incident block. The code therefore provably never changed and the deployment basis is exact (gov/timelock can only retune parameters and swap the external VaultUtils helper, which is configuration rather than a change of the victim's code). Aged-code counterexample: ~1408 days.

limitations: Classification and loss came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/gmx.json; legacy measurement.status=OK is provenance only.
